## What's new in 0.1.4
**Scroll mode opens straight away in long lists.** It used to read every row of a list before showing anything. A Finder list view took up to almost a second, and Notes took more than its time limit, so one of its scroll areas was missing. Both now open in well under a tenth of a second, with every scroll area found.
**Starting a mode from the menu works while Settings is open.** Find Text started from the menu bar with the Settings window open was often dropped without a sign. It now opens over the app you were using.
**Grid Pointer stays readable as the cells shrink.** Once a cell gets too small for its keys, the nine keys move to a keypad beside the selection, and the selection border no longer fills the smallest cells. ⌘R and ⌘C now reach the app instead of picking a cell, and G or ⌘R starts over from the whole screen.
**Click Labels opens faster in Chrome.** Every Chrome activation used to wait about a second and a half before any label appeared. Labels on Chrome's new-tab page now show in under half a second.
**Buttons inside rows and cards get their own label.** A button in a table row or cell, or a small button on a larger one (such as "More actions" on Chrome's profile cards), used to be hidden behind the bigger element's label, so it could not be reached. Both now get a label.
**Smaller fixes.**
- Find Text highlights the right characters after emoji such as flags. Matches used to land one character to the left. - A long pause no longer turns into a huge jump when you scroll by holding a key. - Typing goes back to your app when a display change closes Find Text. - The next-match key in Settings takes the new key you type, and refuses a space. - Turning on screen text warms text recognition up at once. The first search after that is no longer slow. - A Login Item you remove in System Settings stays removed. Settings no longer adds it back. - Buttons that do nothing right now, such as "Check now" in a build with updates off, look disabled.
What has been checked on real apps, and what has not, is recorded in the repository's `docs/COMPATIBILITY-MATRIX.md`.
## Install
Download `KeySearch-0.1.4.dmg`, open it, and drag **KeySearch** to Applications.
**Drag it there — don't run it from the disk image.** macOS ties every permission you grant to the app's *path*. Authorise it while it is still on the mounted image and those grants point at a location that stops existing the moment you eject, with nothing to connect the two. KeySearch warns you if it notices, but moving it first avoids the question.
The first launch is blocked by Gatekeeper — this build is signed, but not with an Apple Developer ID, which needs a paid membership. Open **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, scroll to *Security*, and click **Open Anyway** next to the message about KeySearch. Once only; afterwards it opens normally. (macOS 15 removed the old right-click → Open shortcut, so it is not in that menu.)
**Your permissions survive updates.** Every release is signed with the same certificate, which is what macOS matches when deciding whether an updated app is still the app you authorised.
## Permissions
KeySearch asks for nothing at launch. Each mode requests only what it uses:
| Mode | Needs | | --- | --- | | Find Text | Accessibility or Screen Recording (either one is enough) | | Click Labels, Scroll | Accessibility + Input Monitoring | | Grid Pointer, Free Pointer | Input Monitoring |
Clicking and scrolling anywhere additionally needs event posting. Settings → Permissions lists all four and says which modes each one unlocks.
Requires macOS 14 or newer.
## Verify the download
``` shasum -a 256 -c KeySearch-0.1.4.dmg.sha256 ```
KeySearch has no network connection for app functionality, telemetry or crash reporting. Sparkle only checks the signed update feed when update checks are enabled, and verifies the package before installation.

## What's new in 0.1.3
**Five modes, with plain names.** Click Labels, Scroll, Find Text, Grid Pointer and Free Pointer. Free Pointer used to be a toggle inside Grid; it is now its own mode with its own shortcut, and pressing F in Grid Pointer hands the cursor to it. Grid Pointer now only positions the pointer.
**Click Labels finds more, faster.**
- **Status items in the menu bar get labels.** Each status item belongs to the app that created it, and only the frontmost app's items were read before, so most of them got no label. - **Open menus get labels, and closed ones no longer cost time.** Items of an open menu were clipped to the menu bar and never labelled. Closed menus were walked in full on every pass. On Safari a pass went from about 600 ms to about 50 ms. - **The menu bar is found with a second display attached.** With an extended display, such as an iPad, the menu bar and its items got no labels at all. - **Fewer missing elements.** In some apps, whole parts of the window, sometimes the menu bar, were skipped without any sign. In VS Code, large layout areas covered the controls inside them. That pass is back from 12 labels to 48.
**Find Text no longer comes back empty while macOS is slow to read the screen.** Text recognition sometimes takes from a few seconds to over half a minute, most often the first time after launch. Find Text used to give up at 5 seconds and show no screen text. Now it shows what it has, says it is still reading, and adds the rest when it arrives. The search bar sits at the top of the screen while you type and moves next to the selected match when you step through results with Tab.
**A new look.** A new icon, flat overlays, and one highlight colour that follows your system accent, or one you pick in Settings → General. Settings is now three tabs: Modes, General and Permissions.
What has been checked on real apps, and what has not, is recorded in the repository's `docs/COMPATIBILITY-MATRIX.md`.

## What's new in 0.1.2
**Modes stop silently doing nothing.** Three changes here, all of them cases where the app looked alive and was not:
- **Secure Input now ends a pass in progress.** If another app claims Secure Input — a password field with focus, a password manager, `sudo` — macOS stops delivering keystrokes to Click hints, Scroll and Grid Mouse, including the one that would dismiss the overlay. Those modes now refuse to start while it is held, and a pass already running ends with an explanation instead of an overlay that eats nothing. Search is unaffected: it reads through a text field, not an event tap. The status menu names the condition while it holds. - **Reading the screen is bounded.** Vision has no deadline of its own; a pass that took 63 seconds has been observed, with no text on screen and nothing to explain it. Recognition now runs against a 5-second budget, keeps whatever it read before the deadline, and says the reading was cut short. - **Grid Mouse's help text was wrong in free-cursor mode**, describing the grid's keys ("1–9 select", "F free") while free mode was on. It now states the keys that actually work, and mentions the pinch/rotate gestures only when that experimental setting is on.
**The search panel is now just "Search".** The separate Homerow Search mode was folded into it — one mode that searches accessibility controls and on-screen text together — and the menu, settings and key reference say so. If you had the old mode bound, check Settings → Modes.
**Settings gained a Get started page**, which states the loop once (press the mode's key, narrow to one target, leave with esc), lists every mode with your own key badges, and shows whether each one can start right now — derived from the same check the activation path makes, so a row cannot claim a mode works when it would refuse.
Also in this release: one visual language across every screen (one type scale, one status pill, one key cap, radii named for what they wrap, colours that re-resolve when macOS switches appearance), mode status on the first screen, a recovery path when a mode finds nothing, pointer tuning for Grid Mouse, and a deleted window-source code path that could never run. Full detail is in the repository's `docs/COMPATIBILITY-MATRIX.md`, which records what has been verified on real apps and what has not.
